verdict.rationale: LangSmith documents dashboards that track token usage and can be grouped by run tag or metadata, and it supports cost alerting. Together these give a direct but thinly documented way to split usage by custom attributes. A community comment says capturing which user is involved takes extra work, which affects confidence but is not a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of cost (not just token) breakdowns per user, session, or feature via metadata; documentation of how to attach user, session, or feature metadata to traces; hands-on corroboration of metadata-based cost attribution.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attribute cost and usage to users, sessions, and features via custom metadata

citations.quote: You can use group by run tag or metadata to split data over attributes that are important to your application.
Prebuilt dashboards are created automatically for each project and cover essential metrics, such as trace count, error rates, token usage, and more.
LangSmith provides threshold-based alerting on the following metrics: Run Count, Cost, Errors, Feedback Score, Latency
